Creative Analysis

30 ads · Meta · last 30 days

Split by country · Click any card → public post · Green border = ROAS ≥3 · Yellow = ROAS ≥1.5 · Red = no purch.

🇧🇪

Belgium

30 ads · €11780 spend · 196 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Heart collection statics are the backbone: Heart Tag #2 drives 57 purchases (top volume), Heart White #1 delivers 2.4x ROAS (top efficiency) — the Heart concept resonates hard in Belgium.
• Catalog and carousel formats deliver the lowest CPPs in the account: Carousel (€39.42), Catalog #1 (€42.53), Catalog #2 (€47.23) — multi-product layouts convert efficiently.
• #2 variants consistently outperform #1s: Split #2 (1.68x) vs Split #1 (0.95x), Heart Tag #2 (1.78x) vs Heart Tag #1 (0.89x) — iterative creative testing is paying off.
❌ What's Not Working
• Video creatives are nearly dead in Belgium: Grid #1 and Split #1 delivered zero purchases on €350 combined spend, Tagline #2 managed 0.42x ROAS — only Video Organic #1 survives at 1.52x.
• Static _ Headline #1 is a conversion black hole: highest CTR (153.58%) but 0.64x ROAS and €139.54 CPP — it attracts clicks that never buy.
• Static _ Split #1 burned €1,036 at 0.95x ROAS while its #2 variant outperformed on every metric — slow-to-kill losers are dragging down the account.
⬆ Double Down On
• Heart product statics in every layout variation — the concept converts across White, Tag, Catalog, and Split formats. Produce 3-4 more Heart variants immediately.
• Multi-product catalog and carousel formats — they deliver CPPs 25-40% below account average. Build catalog layouts for every winning concept.
• Aggressive #2/#3 iteration on top performers — Solitaire #1 (2.04x), Summer #2 (1.72x), and iMessage #2 (2.34x) all need fresh variants to find even stronger angles.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• All non-Organic video ads — Video Grid #1, Video Split #1, and Video Tagline #2 combined: €623 spent, 2 purchases, effective ROAS ~0.19x. This format does not work in Belgium.
• Static _ Headline #1 — €698 wasted at 0.64x ROAS. High CTR with no conversion means the creative overpromises and the product page underdelivers.
• Stop running #1 variants once a #2 clearly wins — Split #1 and Heart Tag #1 together wasted €1,205 while their #2 counterparts outperformed them.

kleyo — Ads Report

12 October 2026 · Last 30 days

Meta Ads + Google Ads · Creative insights + Performance

AI

Creative Analysis

30 ads · Meta · last 30 days

Split by country · Click any card → public post · Green border = ROAS ≥3 · Yellow = ROAS ≥1.5 · Red = no results

🇧🇪

Belgium

30 ads · €7937 spend · 111 results
✅ What's Working
• Vergelijking (comparison) format is the undisputed champion — three variants of #2 generated 50 leads combined, best at €47.95/result. Direct broker-vs-kleyo cost framing converts Belgian homeowners consistently.
• Low-spend gems crushing it on CPR: 'Static _ Thomas Guenter #2 - Copy' at €21.96/result, 'Static _ iMessage #1' at €23.55/result, and 'Static _ De Tijd 2' at €23.90/result all prove social proof, conversational, and press-authority formats resonate when creative is sharp.
• Calculation and authority formats ('Static _ Berekening #2' at €51.38, 'Static _ De Tijd 2' at €23.90) show that specific numbers and third-party credibility drive efficient lead gen.
❌ What's Not Working
• Poll format is dead on arrival — 'Static _ Poll #2 - Copy' burned €775 for 4 leads at €193.75/result, 'Static _ Poll #1 - Copy' spent €75 with zero results. Engagement gimmicks don't convert high-consideration real estate decisions.
• iMessage format collapsed under scale — original 'Static _ iMessage #1' hit €23.55/result but the Copy variant at 14x the spend ballooned to €129.68/result. Blindly scaling creative copies without iteration destroys efficiency.
• 'Static _ Review #2 - Copy' (€156.75/result) and 'Static _ Thomas Guenter #2 - Copy 2' (€153 spent, zero results) are pure waste — generic social proof without sharp framing burns budget fast.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce 3-4 new Vergelijking variants: test different home price brackets, swap savings headline angles, try before/after invoice layouts. This format has proven both volume and efficiency — milk it dry.
• Scale the micro-budget winners with disciplined 2x budget increases: Thomas Guenter #2 Copy (€22/result), iMessage #1 original (€24/result), and De Tijd 2 (€24/result) need validation at €200-400 spend before full deployment.
• Create hybrid creatives merging winning elements: comparison layout + real seller face + specific calculation. The data shows comparison converts, social proof builds trust, and numbers close — combine all three.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all Poll variants immediately — both #1 and #2 confirm the format is fundamentally wrong for real estate lead gen. Zero creative runway here.
• Pause 'Static _ iMessage #1 - Copy' now — €1,297 at €130/result while the original does €24/result is indefensible budget misallocation.
• Cut 'Static _ Thomas Guenter #2 - Copy 2' and 'Static _ Review #2 - Copy' — €310 combined spend, one lead total. Dead weight.

🇧🇪

Belgium

21 ads · €1715 spend · 23 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Lifestyle imagery crushes it — 'Static _ Lifestyle #2 - Copy' delivers 10.68x ROAS at €12.90 CPP, proving real-world context sells better than product-on-white.
• Offer-driven creative converts efficiently — 'Static _ Offer #1 - Copy' at 3.4x ROAS and €46 CPP shows price anchoring or promo messaging pulls purchase-ready buyers.
• Colors concept has volume potential — 'Static _ Colors #1' attracted most spend (€707) with 9 purchases, and 'Static _ Colors #2' hit 3.53x ROAS, confirming lens color variety is a compelling hook.
❌ What's Not Working
• Split-format creatives are a dead end — 'Static _ Split #1' and '#2' burned €282 combined with zero purchases. The before/after or side-by-side layout isn't converting.
• HelboF launch creatives got no traction — 6 Helbo Fotochroom ads collectively spent €28 with zero purchases. Meta's algorithm starved them for good reason; the creative concepts aren't compelling enough to compete.
• Vuelta-themed ads are inconsistent — 'Vuelta Full #1' spiked at 6.89x but on only €21; the other three Vuelta variants produced nothing. Event tie-in creative is too niche to scale.
⬆ Double Down On
• Lifestyle/action imagery showing riders wearing NAOS glasses in real Belgian cycling and gravel settings — this is the highest-ROAS format by far.
• Offer and promo-led statics with clear price callouts or bundle deals — the Offer #1 format proves intent capture works, iterate with seasonal hooks.
• Lens color showcase statics — Colors concept is the only one Meta chose to scale AND convert; test more colorway-focused creatives across Ziris and Helbo lines.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all Split-format creatives immediately — €282 wasted, zero signal, the concept is broken.
• Kill the current HelboF creative batch — none are earning spend or conversions. Go back to the drawing board with lifestyle-first Helbo Fotochroom creatives instead of product-only shots.
• Stop spreading budget across 20 statics — consolidate to 8-10 proven and high-potential ads so the algorithm can optimize properly.

Mister Barish — Ads Report

12 October 2026 · Last 30 days

Meta Ads + Google Ads + Klaviyo Email · Creative insights + Performance

AI

Creative Analysis

19 ads · Meta · last 30 days

Split by country · Click any card → public post · Green border = ROAS ≥3 · Yellow = ROAS ≥1.5 · Red = no purch.

🇧🇪

Belgium

19 ads · €1304 spend · 12 purchases
✅ What's Working
• USvThem comparison format is the account hero — the low-spend instance of "Static _ USvThem #1" hit 31.49x ROAS at €17.23 CPP, proving competitive positioning resonates hard with Belgian coffee buyers.
• Social proof converts when done right — "Static _ Review #1" delivered 16.59x ROAS and "Static _ Schema #1" hit 5.74x, both on tiny spend begging to be scaled.
• Video Routine format drives massive engagement and early conversion signal — "Video _ Routine #1" posted 18.03x ROAS on first purchase, and "Video _ Routine #2" has the highest CTR in the account at 253.58%.
❌ What's Not Working
• Search concept is a money pit — two instances of "Static _ Search #1" burned €426 combined for 2 purchases at sub-0.4x ROAS. The creative promise doesn't match post-click intent.
• Chat format flatlines on conversion — both "Static _ Chat #1" instances spent €45 combined with zero purchases despite strong CTRs, suggesting the conversational angle attracts curious browsers, not buyers.
• Winners degrade at scale — "Static _ Review #2" drops from 3.73x to 0.51x ROAS and "Static _ USvThem #1" from 31.49x to 2.8x when spend increases, pointing to audience saturation or poor broad targeting at higher budgets.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more USvThem/comparison statics — this is the highest-conviction format in the account. Test new comparison angles: Mister Barish beans vs supermarket brands, curated machines vs random Amazon picks, specialty vs commodity coffee.
• Scale video Routine content aggressively — morning ritual / espresso-making videos drive unmatched engagement and show early conversion; create variations featuring different blends (ZERO, WILD, GOLD) and machine pairings.
• Mine the review/testimonial vein deeper — "Static _ Review #1" and "Static _ Schema #1" both convert profitably at low CPP. Create more social-proof statics with real customer quotes, star ratings, and before/after coffee upgrade stories.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill both "Static _ Search #1" instances immediately — €426 wasted at 0.36x ROAS or worse. The concept is broken, not the audience.
• Kill both "Static _ Chat #1" instances — engagement without conversion is vanity. €45 spent, zero purchases.
• Stop letting winning creatives bleed at high spend without frequency caps or audience refreshes — the €337 "Static _ Review #2" and €307 "Static _ USvThem #1" instances prove the algorithm will happily waste budget on exhausted audiences.

🇧🇪

Belgium

12 ads · €1045 spend · 0 results
✅ What's Working
• Sky-high CTRs across all angles (Myth, USvsTHEM, General) — creative is clearly stopping thumbs and generating clicks.
• Myth-busting angle pulls strongest engagement: 'Static _ Myth #2' hits 72-114% CTR, 'Static _ Myth #1' hits 69-72% CTR — the concept resonates in Belgium.
• USvsTHEM competitive positioning drives the most Meta spend allocation (€731 across variants), suggesting the algorithm sees engagement signals worth bidding on.
❌ What's Not Working
• Zero conversions across €1,044 total spend — every single euro is wasted. This is a catastrophic post-click or tracking failure, not a creative problem.
• CTRs of 60-114% are abnormally high, suggesting either 'all clicks' is being reported instead of link CTR, or the conversion event/pixel is completely broken in Belgium.
• The entire Belgium market is running only static formats — no video, no carousels, no instant forms — leaving massive format diversity untested while burning budget on a broken funnel.
⬆ Double Down On
• Fix the funnel FIRST: audit pixel firing, conversion event setup, and landing page for Belgian visitors before spending another euro — the data screams tracking failure.
• Myth-busting angle for Belgium: highest CTRs consistently — produce more myth variants addressing Belgian-specific EV charging concerns (grid capacity, apartment living, subsidies).
• Test Meta Instant Forms to bypass the landing page entirely — if the LP is the bottleneck, lead forms will diagnose and solve simultaneously.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop all current Belgium spend immediately until conversion tracking is verified — €1,044 with zero results is not a creative problem, it's a measurement or funnel problem.
• Kill the assumption that static-only creative is sufficient — Belgium needs format testing (video, carousel, instant forms) alongside the tracking fix.
• Stop duplicating the same ad names across ad sets without differentiation — it's creating confusion in reporting and making optimization impossible.

Belgium

1 ads · €153 spend · 6 results
✅ What's Working
• "Static _ Investeren _ 2" delivers leads at €25.49 — solid for Belgian real estate lead gen with minimal spend.
• Investment angle resonates: the 'Investeren' framing clearly hooks financially-motivated buyers seeking Zeeland property.
• Static format is pulling results cheaply at low spend — proven entry point before scaling.
❌ What's Not Working
• Only ONE ad running across all of Belgium — zero creative diversity means zero learning and massive audience fatigue risk.
• No lifestyle, emotional, or waterfront-dream creative exists despite the brand's core positioning being rust, water, and panoramic views.
• No video, carousel, or dynamic formats tested — relying entirely on a single static is leaving performance on the table.
⬆ Double Down On
• Investment-angle statics with sharper hooks — the '100% verhuurgarantie' and 'rendement aan het water' angles are untapped goldmines for Belgian investors.
• Dreamy lifestyle video content: drone shots of Westerschelde, golden-hour kijkwoning walkthroughs, morning-coffee-with-panoramic-view moments.
• Belgian-specific second-home messaging — 'uw tweede thuis op 1u van Antwerpen' type geo-proximity hooks that collapse the distance objection.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill the one-ad-fits-all approach immediately — you cannot run a real estate lead gen campaign in Belgium on a single static and expect scalable results.
• Stop ignoring the kijkwoning asset — it's the strongest conversion trigger in the funnel and zero ads reference it as a CTA.

Netherlands

3 ads · €270 spend · 7 results
✅ What's Working
• Video _ Lifestyle #1 crushes it at €15.50 CPR with highest CTR (426%) — lifestyle-driven, emotive creative clearly resonates with Dutch waterfront dreamers.
• Static _ Water Wind _ Form delivers volume (4 leads) with evocative water/wind imagery — the dreamy, nature-first angle lands well in this market.
• Lead-gen CTRs across the board are unusually high, suggesting the Waterzande proposition itself has strong pull — creative just needs to not get in the way.
❌ What's Not Working
• Static _ Investeren _ 2 - Copy is bleeding money at €86.24 CPR — rational investment messaging in static format fails to convert Dutch prospects who want to feel the lifestyle first.
• Static creative overall underperforms video by 2.5-5.5x on CPR — the waterfront story needs motion, sound, and atmosphere that stills can't deliver.
• No creative diversity in the funnel — only 3 ads running means zero creative testing velocity and heavy fatigue risk.
⬆ Double Down On
• Lifestyle video is the clear winner format — produce more short-form video showcasing water, golden hour light on the Westerschelde, and the feeling of space and rust.
• Nature-first emotional hooks (water, wind, panoramic views) outperform rational investment angles — lead with feeling, convert with facts in the landing page.
• Lean into the kijkwoning CTA — give people a tangible next step tied to aspirational imagery to keep CPR low.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop running investment-angle statics — Static _ Investeren _ 2 - Copy has spent €86 for a single lead; the rational pitch in a cold static is dead on arrival.
• Stop spreading budget thinly across underperforming statics when video is 5.5x more efficient — consolidate spend behind what converts.

Other

26 ads · €5601 spend · 174 results
✅ What's Working
• 'Water Wind _ Form' and 'Nieuw_App #1' are the clear CPR champions — €9.31 and €7.43 respectively. Water/apartment-forward creative with inline forms crushes.
• 'Video #2' quietly delivers at €8.38/result with the highest CTR (732%) on minimal spend — video format has untapped potential.
• USP-lite and concise property-focused ads ('USP #2' at €20.14, 'Investeren - Copy 2' at €17.78) outperform heavy-text or dreamy approaches.
❌ What's Not Working
• The 'Dreamer' angle is dead — both 'Dreamer #2' variants (€153 + €41) returned zero results, and 'Dreamer #1' costs €87.54/lead. Aspirational fluff without specifics doesn't convert.
• 'Investeren' full-format ads are money pits — 'Investeren _ 3 - Copy 2' burned €263 for zero leads, 'Investeren _ Full #1' at €119.57/lead, 'Investeren _ Full #2' at €32 with nothing.
• Top-spend ads 'Review _ Form' (€77/lead) and 'Opsomming #2' (€51.71/lead) are eating budget at 5-10x the CPR of winners — Meta is optimizing for spend, not results.
⬆ Double Down On
• Apartment-specific creatives with clear product news ('Nieuw_App' angle) — the best CPR by far. Create more variants with different visuals and copy hooks.
• Water/nature imagery paired with form-based CTAs ('Water Wind _ Form' model) — 62 leads at €9.31 proves this is the scalable format.
• Video content — 'Video #2' at €8.38/result with 732% CTR on just €42 spend is begging for budget. Produce more short-form video with water/panorama footage.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all 'Dreamer' creatives immediately — the romantic/evocative angle generates clicks but zero conversions.
• Kill all 'Investeren _ Full' and 'Investeren _ 3' variants — hard investment framing repels this audience.
• Slash budget on 'Review _ Form' and 'Opsomming #2' — together they've spent €2,319 for 37 leads at €62.67 avg CPR while better ads are starved of budget.

Belgium

21 ads · €1099 spend · 93 results
✅ What's Working
• Naoshima #2 (€6.17 CPR, 23 results) and Sommerfeld #3 (€6.15 CPR, 21 results) are clear efficiency leaders — both deliver high volume at sub-€7 cost per lead.
• Original Sommerfeld #2 achieves the lowest CPR in the set at €4.91, proving the Sommerfeld creative direction resonates strongly even at low spend.
• Bauhaus #2 is the reliable volume workhorse — highest spend (€209), 18 results, and a respectable €11.64 CPR that holds under budget pressure.
❌ What's Not Working
• Copy variants are systematically destroying efficiency: Sommerfeld #2 - Copy (€25.90) is 5× worse than its original (€4.91); Sommerfeld #1 - Copy burns €93 for just 2 leads at €46.53 each.
• The entire Sommerfeld #1 creative concept is dead — both original and copy combined spent €94 for only 2 results. Whatever this visual is, it doesn't convert.
• Naoshima is massively under-explored: only 2 ads, one of which (Naoshima #1) got zero clicks at 0% CTR. Your best-performing creative direction has almost no variants to learn from.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce 3-4 new Naoshima-style creatives immediately — this direction has the best efficiency-to-volume ratio and is starved of variants for Meta to optimize against.
• Double budget on proven originals (Sommerfeld #2, Sommerfeld #3) and kill their underperforming Copy duplicates to consolidate learnings.
• Introduce video and carousel formats — every single ad is a static; you're leaving format-level optimization entirely on the table for a visually rich architectural product.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all Sommerfeld #1 variants now. Both ads combined: €94 spent, 2 results, €47 avg CPR. The creative is broken.
• Stop duplicating ads as '-Copy' without meaningful creative changes. Five of six Copy variants underperform their originals — you're splitting budget into worse-performing clones.
• Pause Naoshima #1 — 0% CTR means the creative is dead on arrival. Don't let it contaminate the Naoshima ad set.

Belgium

29 ads · €1158 spend · 34 results
✅ What's Working
• B2B creative is the only category converting — top 3 ads (4 Momenten #1, Açai Koffiebar, Boost #2) generated 31 of 33 total results on €658 combined spend
• Occasion-based B2B messaging dominates: "Static _ B2B _ 4 Momenten #1" delivered the best cost/result at €14.28 by framing açai across daily serving moments
• Practical integration angles (coffee bar setup, menu addition, brunch upgrade) consistently drive high engagement from hospitality decision-makers
❌ What's Not Working
• Every single B2C consumer ad produced zero results — €300+ wasted across 11 creatives including Notes, Deinze, Organic, Carrousel, Wekker, Craving, OldvsNew, and Reminder variants
• Static-only B2C creative is completely failing: consumer CTRs average 1–4% with no mechanism to drive viewers to Bio-Planet or Delhaize
• No endorser leverage, no retail store CTA, no video — B2C creatives have zero hook for health-conscious consumers and zero path to purchase
⬆ Double Down On
• B2B occasion/moment-based concepts — iterate on the "4 Momenten" framework with day-part, menu-section, and use-case variants
• Build B2C video content featuring endorsers (Bekkari, Gruyaert, Dr. Servaas Binge) with explicit "Available at Bio-Planet & Delhaize" CTAs — static alone is not working
• Develop B2C creatives that bridge awareness to physical retail: store locator visuals, in-store photography, and proximity-triggered messaging
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• All 11 current B2C static consumer ads — zero combined results, no salvageable signal anywhere in the batch
• Both "Notes" variants immediately — Notes #1 had literally 0% CTR and Notes #2 burned €98 for absolutely nothing
• Stop running any B2C creative that doesn't include a clear retail purchase path or store-level call to action

Belgium

2 ads · €88 spend · 0 results
✅ What's Working
• Both ads (120239394435940631 and 120239393986810631) generate absurdly high CTRs (150%+), suggesting strong curiosity or engagement bait — people are clicking, just not converting.
• Some level of creative intrigue exists; the hook is clearly catching attention in-feed even if nothing downstream works.
❌ What's Not Working
• Zero results on both ads despite €87 total spend — 120239394435940631 burned €57 with nothing to show. The funnel after the click is completely broken.
• Sky-high CTRs with zero conversions screams landing page mismatch, wrong campaign objective, or broken tracking. Clicks mean nothing if the destination doesn't convert.
• Likely running traffic or engagement objective instead of conversion-optimized campaigns — Meta is finding clickers, not buyers.
⬆ Double Down On
• Fix the foundation first: verify pixel/CAPI tracking, confirm conversion events fire correctly, and audit the landing page for Dutch-speaking B2B buyers before any new spend.
• Lean into the engagement energy — the hooks clearly work. Repurpose that creative angle into proper conversion-optimized campaigns with a clear CTA (quote request, catalog download).
• Build a B2B lead gen funnel: workwear buyers need quotes, customization info, and bulk pricing — give them a frictionless way to request it.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop running campaigns without verified conversion tracking — every euro is flying blind right now.
• Kill any traffic/engagement objectives immediately. A B2B workwear company needs leads or purchases, not clicks to nowhere.

Belgium

30 ads · €1371 spend · 46 results
✅ What's Working
• Square format "-Copy" variants are dominant: "Static _ Square #1 - Copy" (€11.44/result, 11 results) and "Static _ Square #2 - Copy" (€10.77/result, 8 results) are the most efficient ads in the account.
• Split "-Copy" variants also perform well: "Static _ Split #2 - Copy" delivers 9 results at €12.46 each — the copy refresh clearly outperforms originals across all formats.
• High-volume + low-cost creatives cluster in the Square and Split Copy variants, proving that format + iteration matters more than spend level.
❌ What's Not Working
• The entire Conservative creative line is a money pit: 6 ads, €380 total spend, only 1 result at €167.92. "Static_Conservative #2" burned €74 for zero results.
• Original (non-Copy) creatives consistently underperform their Copy counterparts — "Static _ Split #2" costs €56.31/result vs its Copy at €12.46. The originals are dead weight.
• Popout format is mediocre at best: €225 across 5 Popout ads yielded only 6 results, with 3 of 5 variants producing zero.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more Square-format static variations — this format has the lowest cost/result and highest volume. Iterate on the winning "Copy" angles with new hooks, colors, and CTAs.
• Create more Split-format variations modeled on the "-Copy" winners. Test new headline structures and benefit-forward messaging in the same layout.
• Invest in conversion tracking: ROAS is missing across all 20 ads. Without revenue data, you're flying blind on actual profitability. Set up value-based optimization immediately.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill every Conservative creative immediately. Six ads, one garbage result. This design direction is proven dead in Belgium.
• Kill all original (non-Copy) versions of Square, Split, and Popout — the originals are outspent and outperformed by their refreshed counterparts across the board.

🇧🇪

Belgium

30 ads · €4536 spend · 27 results
✅ What's Working
• "Static _ Poll #2" and "Static _ LinkedIn #1" deliver the lowest cost/result (€17.61 and €20.39) — engagement and authority-proof angles clearly resonate in this market.
• "Static _ Rip #1" (€876 spend) is the volume workhorse with 12 results, proving the "rip" concept has legs even at €72.97/result.
• "Static _ Notes #1" (€183 version) quietly converts at €36.51/result with 5 results — educational/utility framing works.
❌ What's Not Working
• The "Business #1" creative is an absolute money pit — three instances totaling €1,891 in spend with zero results. Dead concept, dead hook.
• "Static _ Mail #1" burned €152 with nothing. "Static _ Notes #2" spent €79 with nothing. Variants of working concepts aren't automatically winners.
• No ROAS tracking anywhere — you're flying blind on actual revenue. Without this, you cannot optimize toward profitable scale.
⬆ Double Down On
• Interactive/engagement hooks: Poll and LinkedIn proof-style creatives convert cheapest. Build a family of 3-4 variants around social proof, polls, and community validation.
• "Rip" concept variations: It's the only concept with double-digit conversions. Create new angles, video adaptations, and fresh hooks around this proven winner.
• Utility/educational framing: "Notes #1" works because it likely provides value upfront. Expand into how-to, walkthrough, and tip-style statics.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill every "Business #1" instance immediately — €1,891 wasted across three duplicates with zero conversions. The concept is dead.
• Kill "Static _ Mail #1" — €152, zero results, no signal worth chasing.
• Stop running duplicate ad names in parallel without differentiation — it fragments learning and wastes budget on the same losing creative.

30 ads · €9615 spend · 125 results
✅ What's Working
• Animation format dominates — "Vottem_animatie" delivers €27.71 CPR across 12 results, cheapest leads in the entire account by a wide margin.
• Remarketing native is the secret weapon — "stokerie_int_v1_rem - native" at €34.24 CPR outperforms cold "stokerie_int_native" (€57.15) by 40%, proving warm audiences + native placement is the winning formula.
• Terrain/exterior-first creative pulls volume — "awans_terrain_v1" (€43.46, 13 results) and "Brugge_penthouse" (€47.04, 10 results) show that leading with the product and location beats abstract or interior-only angles.
❌ What's Not Working
• Wildebeek is completely dead — 3 ads, €786 combined spend, 1 total result. "wildebeek_int" and "ODD Wildenbeek 1/10/26" both at zero results. No creative format is saving this.
• Charleroi has no pulse — "Charleroi_te-huur" burned €250 for zero results, "Charleroi_native" costs €256.53 per result. The market or the offer simply isn't landing.
• "West" format sprawl is killing efficiency — "west_kijkapt_native" (€184 CPR) and "west_video" (€131 CPR) hemorrhage budget while "west_ext" alone delivers 10 results at €61. Wrong formats dragging down a viable project.
⬆ Double Down On
• Roll out animation format (Vottem_animatie style) to every active project — Brugge, Awans, Stokerie, Georges. The 3D walkthrough/animation creative converts at 2-3x better than static or standard video across the board.
• Build remarketing native layers for all projects with proven cold traffic — Stokerie rem format already proves it. Replicate for Vottem, Brugge, and Awans where cold ads are generating volume to retarget.
• Double down on terrain/exterior/location-first creative — outdoor shots, building progress, and neighborhood context consistently outperform interiors-only or abstract creative. Lead every new ad with what the buyer actually sees.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all 3 Wildebeek ads immediately — €786 for 1 result is indefensible. Either the project lacks market demand or needs a complete strategy reset before any more spend.
• Kill "Charleroi_te-huur" — zero results, rental angle is dead in this market. "Charleroi_native" should follow unless a fresh creative test proves otherwise.
• Kill "west_kijkapt_native" and "west_video" — €815 combined for 5 results while "west_ext" alone does 10 for €612. Consolidate West budget behind the one format that works.

Belgium

30 ads · €3421 spend · 61 results
✅ What's Working
• "Doorstromer #1 - Copy" is the clear winner: 22 results at €13.19 each on only €290 spend — massively outperforming every other ad.
• "Alleenstaand #2" delivers nearly identical efficiency (16 results, €13.43/result) proving the single-person audience segment converts.
• The original creative versions consistently outperform their V2 reworks — the V2 refresh likely diluted what was working.
❌ What's Not Working
• "Doorstromer V2 #1" is burning €1,491 (46% of total spend) at a horrific €135.52/result — 10x worse than the Copy variant of the same concept. This is the #1 budget leak.
• General/Algemeen targeting is dead: "General V2 #1" spent €205 with zero results; both Algemeen variants also returned nothing. Broad targeting doesn't convert for Zabrixx.
• Jong Koppel, ODD, Ticket, Split, Notification, and Melding concepts are collectively €336 spent with exactly zero results across 8 ads.
⬆ Double Down On
• Doorstromer audience with original (non-V2) creative treatment — replicate the winning formula of "Doorstromer #1 - Copy" with new angles, hooks, and visuals.
• Alleenstaand audience segment — only 2 ads have meaningful spend; this is undertested and clearly converts at scale-worthy CPAs.
• Static format with direct, segment-specific messaging — every result in the account comes from ads that name a specific life stage (Doorstromer, Alleenstaand), not generic appeals.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all V2 reworks that underperform originals — the "refresh" strategy backfired across Doorstromer and Alleenstaand segments.
• Kill every zero-result concept immediately: Jong Koppel, ODD, Ticket, Melding, Split, Notification, Algemeen, General — €541 wasted with nothing to show.
• Stop spreading budget across 20 ads. Consolidate into 5-6 proven performers to give the algorithm real signal.

• "Visual | Wedstrijd" delivers strong volume (45 results) proving that competition/giveaway mechanics remain the most reliable engagement driver for provincial government pages.
• Static image formats consistently crush video across every campaign — image ads produce results, video ads burn budget.
❌ What's Not Working
• The entire "Levenslang Leren" campaign is dead on arrival: 10 ad variants, ~€89 total spend, exactly 1 result. The creative angle, messaging, or targeting is fundamentally broken.

• "Onthaalmedewerker - Duinpanne - Image" costs €23.33/result for a recruitment ad — too expensive for a single-image approach to a niche job posting.
⬆ Double Down On
• Image-first creative for all civic engagement and event campaigns — the data is overwhelming; skip video unless there's a strong hypothesis to test.
• Competition/wedstrijd mechanics paired with strong local visuals — this is your proven volume play; create more seasonal and thematic variations.
• Hyper-local, action-oriented campaigns (like Zwin cleanup) with clear calls to participate — specificity drives results, vague "lifelong learning" messaging does not.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all 10 "Levenslang Leren" ads in their current form — they need a complete creative and strategic overhaul before re-launching.
• Kill video as a default format — every video ad underperforms its image counterpart; stop splitting budget 50/50 and lead with static.
• Kill the "Visual | 2" ad at €18.06/result — it's nearly double the cost of "Visual | 1" with no clear upside.

12 ads · €484 spend · 0 results
✅ What's Working
• Reels format drives outsized engagement — 'Post
• Reel Sheary-Tom' (814% CTR) and 'Bericht: Je meest geliefde Marie Jo fit...' (1052% CTR) show the audience responds to motion/product storytelling.
• Event-driven urgency copy resonates — 'Bericht: OPENDEURDAGEN! 😍' (758% CTR) and 'Instagram-bericht: Welkom in onze winkel...' (820% CTR) show local-event framing sparks high engagement.
• Brand-name lingerie references (Marie Jo, PrimaDonna) clearly hook the audience — product-specific posts outperform generic fashion copy on engagement.
❌ What's Not Working
• ZERO results tracked across ALL 12 ads totaling ~€484 in spend. This is not a creative problem — it is a catastrophic campaign setup and tracking failure. Likely boosted posts with no conversion objective, no Pixel/CAPI firing, and no purchase event configured.
• High CTRs over 100% confirm these are engagement/interaction metrics, NOT link clicks. No traffic is being driven to a conversion point. Every euro is buying likes, not revenue.
• Static 'Instagram-bericht' posts like 'Sexy en stijlvol in zwart' (€35, 0 results) and 'Weekend van de Klant' (€45, 0 results) are just organic posts with money behind them — no ad architecture whatsoever.
⬆ Double Down On
• Rebuild top-engagement creatives (Marie Jo, Sheary-Tom Reel, OPENDEURDAGEN) inside proper Sales/Conversion campaigns with functioning Pixel + CAPI and a purchase objective. The creative resonance is there — the plumbing is not.
• Produce short-form Reels (5-15s) showcasing product try-ons and fitting expertise — the two Reel-format ads massively outperformed statics on engagement, suggesting strong format-audience fit for lingerie.
• Lean into event/urgency hooks (open door days, weekend van de klant) but pair them with a clear landing page, discount code tracking, and a single CTA driving to shop — turn engagement bait into conversion machines.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop boosting organic posts immediately. Every ad here is a boosted post burning budget with no conversion path. Build ads in Ads Manager with proper campaign objectives.
• Kill any ad spend until Meta Pixel and Conversions API are verified firing on the website. €484 has been donated to Meta with zero measurable return.
